source.title: Demystifying Variance in Circuit Discovery of LLMs
source.authors: F. Wu; Francesco Tonin; V. Cevher

record.tranche_reason: The study reports IOI circuit evaluations and finds template-dependent circuits, qualifying the idea that one comprehensive circuit explains the task across prompt variants.
record.gate_note: The study cites the original IOI circuit paper but reports its own CEAP circuit-discovery results on IOI. It does not test the named 26-head circuit or head roles. Other results on SVA, greater-than, and sparse code models were not treated as IOI findings.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own CEAP circuit discovery on IOI prompts for GPT-2 small and Pythia-160M and finds that per-sample circuits differ by template. This bears on V6, the claim that one mechanism carries IOI across prompt variants. It also argues that per-sample unfaithfulness is inflated by normalization, which bears on V5. It does not examine the 26-head circuit or its head classes.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct but incomplete. The authors conclude that different templates activate different circuits, across SVA, IOI and greater-than, so comprehensive task circuits may be unattainable and steering unreliable. They also conclude that CEAP reduces resampling variance and that sparse training does not merge template circuits. Finally, extreme per-sample unfaithfulness is largely a normalization artifact ('selective contribution scaling'), not a sign of defective circuits.
record.recipe_differences: Uses conductance-based EAP (CEAP) to score edges and evaluates patched subgraphs with unfaithfulness and pairwise Jaccard overlap; the original claim concerns a manually analyzed 26-head circuit and its head roles.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI circuit overlap varies across prompt templates. The reported GPT-2 small IOI average unfaithfulness is for a fixed circuit size of 6000 edges; the paper notes this is the maximum size tested for that visualization.

fits_no_version.finding: For IOI, edge-level circuits from EAP-IG change when the 1000-sample probe set is resampled. CEAP gives pairwise Jaccard index equal or higher in GPT-2 small/XL and Pythia-160M/2.8B, with comparable unfaithfulness (Figures 11, 17, 23, 29).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attribution-patching circuit discovery on IOI is unstable under data resampling, and the instability depends on the scoring method.

record.problems: The IOI overlap evidence is presented as a figure without exact pairwise values. The unfaithfulness result concerns CEAP-discovered edge circuits, not the original 26-head circuit or its class-specific causal roles.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed CEAP and EAP-IG IOI unfaithfulness curves by template and edge count in Appendix F, Figures 23–24, were not extracted as separate figure-only rows; the text does not give their per-template values, and the explicit IOI summary and template-overlap result are recorded in r1–r2.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, their 7 classes and roles, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria for that circuit are not examined.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no test of backup heads or self-repair.
IOI circuit stability is run on GPT-2 XL, Pythia-2.8B and Pythia-160M, but head classes and roles are never compared across models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse for other tasks is not tested.

CEAP and EAP-IG are compared only on resampling stability and unfaithfulness curves, not on whether they recover the same circuit. KL divergence is said to give qualitatively similar results, but no numbers are shown.
No prompts with more than two names. No head-level or role-level comparison across templates, only edge-set overlap.

missing.what: Pythia-160M IOI per-sample circuit overlap across the 14 templates at 2313 edges, average unfaithfulness 0.200, PJI scale about 0.25–0.50; described as template-induced circuit difference

Spearman diagnostics linking per-sample unfaithfulness to |QG|, score heavy-tailedness and included score mass, extended to all IOI templates for GPT-2 small and Pythia-160M; the authors say the trends hold
IOI resampling PJI and unfaithfulness curves by template for GPT-2 XL, Pythia-2.8B and Pythia-160M; rows_left_out only declares the GPT-2 small curves

record.verdict_notes: The template-dependence evidence for IOI is weaker than for SVA. SVA shows two groups with near-zero overlap; the IOI matrices show moderate overlap throughout. GPT-2 small IOI is also the one case where the circuit never reached unfaithfulness below 0.2. All circuits are automatically found edge sets, so none of this speaks directly to the original head classes.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates CEAP-discovered edge circuits on GPT-2 small IOI, but does not test the specified 26-head circuit, its seven head classes and roles, or the authors' faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria for that exact circuit.
The study does not ablate main name-mover heads or test self-repair by backup heads.

Although IOI experiments include other models, the study does not test whether the specified head classes and roles carry IOI across models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether those components are reused for other tasks.
The study compares CEAP and EAP-IG on circuit stability and unfaithfulness, but does not measure whether different methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
The IOI results assess template variation and circuit unfaithfulness, but do not comprehensively vary ablation type or evaluation metric for the specified head circuit.
The study tests IOI prompt templates, including ABBA and BABA forms, but does not test prompts with more than two names or establish that the same components carry IOI across all possible templates.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated CEAP-discovered IOI circuits using unfaithfulness across samples; the reported aggregate is for a circuit with 6000 edges.

conditions.value: 6000 (maximum tested; about 20% of all possible edges)
all samples in the reported GPT-2 small IOI visualization

rows.note: The study states that average unfaithfulness remains above 0.2 even at this maximum tested circuit size. This is an evaluation of its discovered circuits, not the original named 26-head circuit.
rows.check: Remove the V1 link. The circuit is a 6000-edge CEAP edge circuit (about 20% of edges), not the 26-head circuit, so it says nothing about that circuit's faithfulness, completeness or minimality. The 0.240 is a per-sample average (outer expectation). The authors argue this form is inflated by samples with small |QG|, so it reads as evidence that apparent faithfulness depends on the metric, not as a clean measure of incompleteness.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Compared sample-level circuit overlap across IOI prompt templates using pairwise Jaccard index.
rows.measure: Pairwise Jaccard index between circuits from different samples/templates
rows.note: The paper presents the overlap matrix and describes its results as template-induced circuit differences. The figure indicates overlap is not uniformly absent, so it does not establish completely disjoint circuits.
rows.check: Drop the V5 link: this row measures whether circuit identity changes with template, not how faithful the circuit looks under an evaluation choice. Figure 34's colour scale runs about 0.30–0.55, so overlap is moderate, not near zero as in the SVA case. The union of the 6000-edge circuits covers 24711 of 32491 edges. Overlap is between edge sets, not head roles, and within-template variation is mixed in with between-template differences.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small IOI, 14 two-name templates (ABBA/BABA × 7 phrasings), per-sample CEAP circuits of 6000 edges
relationships.reason: Per-sample circuit overlap is only moderate (PJI about 0.30–0.55) and the authors describe template-induced circuit differences. The prompt template thus changes which edges carry IOI, though overlap is far from zero and roles are not compared (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Per-sample circuits had PJI overlap of approximately 0.30–0.55, and template changes altered which edges carried IOI.
